text:
Anya: Heads-up — need to recalibrate RICE for Q2 roadmap. Enterprise legal just signed a PoC but they're asking SLA 99.9 + KMS + single-tenant. Should we bump Dedicated path? cc @Marta @Liam
Marta: If we take them, the revenue upside is real. My gut: impact is large but effort for full private/KMS is nontrivial. :thinking_face:
Liam: Can we split the work? Ship a PoC slice with KMS + a reduced SLA (99.5) and defer full private network isolation until after commitment. That lowers immediate effort and risk.
Devon: Agree with split. Sequencing matters — prioritizing SLA now will delay batching/Optimize work which reduces unit cost. Tradeoffs all over.
Raj: From the customer: they're willing to accept a staged approach — PoC requires 99.5 + KMS, production expects 99.9 and single-tenant later. Gives us runway.
Anya: OK, that suggests two RICE lines: 1) "SLA+KMS for PoC" and 2) "Private full-prod rollout". We should recompute scores and add a strategic tiebreaker for revenue-qualified deals.
Marta: Quick sketch of numbers — propose we start with estimates and iterate. Impact (subjective) I=8 for SLA+KMS, Reach=2 (pilot customers), Confidence=0.6, Effort=3. Can someone do the calc?
Liam: Quick calc: R*I*C/E = (2*8*0.6)/3 = 3.2 — low absolute but strategic.
Devon: For contrast, Optimize perf work (batching/quantization) rough: Reach=100, Impact=2, Conf=0.7, Effort=10 => (100*2*0.7)/10 = 14.
Marta: So perf work wins numerically, but RICE misses strategic capture and runway for enterprise expansion. We need a secondary axis for "strategic revenue capture".
Anya: Proposal: Keep numeric RICE but apply a gating multiplier for commercial-qualified customers. If projected ARR > $150k, add a +1.5 multiplier to the SLA slice score, or just mark it as "escalate to exec review". Thoughts?
Raj: Customer potential is ~ $180k ARR if they convert after PoC, so it crosses that threshold.
product-bot: poll created — "Prioritize SLA+KMS PoC over Optimize perf this quarter?" Options: Yes / No / Need more data. Poll link: https://redwood.internal/polls/4821
Anya: Minimal SLA spec to scope PoC (draft):
```
- 99.5% availability across target region
- KMS w/ customer-managed key (bring-your-own-key)
- isolated routing for tenant (not full on-prem network)
- canary rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 100% with rollback hooks
- audit logs + token-level billing visibility
```
Marta: That seems doable as a narrow slice. Effort estimate drops if we limit isolation to routing + IAM and postpone full VPC-onboarding.
Liam: I'll sketch the PoC implementation plan and call out compatibility with our Dedicated/Dedicated+Private layers. Will include rollback and fallback to hosted models.
Devon: I'll model the ops cost delta and perf risk (latency tail) for the PoC path vs investing in batching.
Raj: I'll confirm exact customer timeline and whether they can start PoC in 4 weeks. If yes, that's our deadline.
Anya: Action items: Marta draft minimal SLA spec doc and gate criteria, Liam scope PoC impl plan, Devon ops cost model, Raj customer timeline confirmation. Reconvene Fri 11am to finalize RICE updates and decide whether to escalate. :+1:
Marta: Sounds good. If poll trends Yes, I'll prepare a short exec note on revenue impact and recommended tradeoffs.
product-bot: poll results so far: 4 Yes, 1 No, 1 Need more data.
Anya: Great — thanks all. We'll keep the perf work in the backlog but treat the SLA PoC as time-boxed and dependent on customer signal.
Liam: Adding link to current RICE sheet: https://docs.redwood/intern/rice/q2-2026 (please update your rows)
Anya: End of thread.
